note: Cited to a pinned Wikipedia revision (trusted_secondary): Pole of inaccessibility (its Point Nemo section). claims.text: Point Nemo, the oceanic pole of inaccessibility, is roughly at 48°52.6′S 123°23.6′W and is the place in the ocean that is farthest from land.
It is equidistant from the three closest landmasses, which are each roughly 2,688 km away.
The three are Pandora Islet of the Ducie Island atoll (Pitcairn Islands), Motu Nui (adjacent to Easter Island) and Maher Island (near Siple Island, off Marie Byrd Land, Antarctica).
It was first identified in 1992 by Croatian survey engineer Hrvoje Lukatela and named Point Nemo, Latin for 'nobody', after Captain Nemo from Jules Verne's novel.

The wider area is known as a spacecraft cemetery: hundreds of decommissioned satellites and spacecraft have been made to fall there; the International Space Station is planned to crash near Point Nemo in 2031.
